nodes.label: Sign is set by evaluation shift: state hurts out of the training range, is neutral-to-helpful in distribution.
The harm comes from absolute frames (and velocity terms); relative or grounded state helps under any evaluation.
Naive fusion lets state dominate optimisation and suppress vision; with regularised/grounded fusion state helps.
State helps when cameras miss task-relevant information (single fixed view, bimanual relations); redundant with full wrist views.
No general factor: effects are task- and setup-specific noise.
Sign is set by the TYPE of shift: state hurts when the robot/scene configuration leaves the training range, helps when the cameras fail.

State hurts only under configuration shift AND raw (absolute, naive) encoding; corrected frame or regularised fusion makes it help there; it helps under camera faults; neutral-to-helpful in distribution.
